paragraphs: A local web app that talks to the xah.io OpenAI-compatible API and renders answers the way coding assistants do: streamed markdown, syntax-highlighted code blocks, a copy button on every snippet, and a Files button that zips every file in an answer.

It is multi-user: each person signs up, pastes their own sk- key, and every request is signed with that key, so the operator never spends their own balance. Prices come from the provider's own model catalogue, and an admin panel shows real spend per user and per model.

Calling the API straight from the browser does not work here: the endpoint sends no CORS headers, and a static page would have to embed each secret key where anyone could read it. server.js sits in between — or api/index.js, the same routes packaged as one Vercel function — holds keys only in the encrypted database, and rebuilds every chat body from a whitelist of recognised parameters, so it cannot be abused as an open relay to the rest of the upstream API.
features: Streaming answers over SSE, with a live caret and a Stop button that also cancels the
upstream request, so you stop paying for tokens you will not read.
One-click code copy. Every block has a language label, a Copy button, and a Download button
that names the file from the block's language or a leading comment (// filename: src/a.js, or a bare # path/to/file.py).
